title: Market Conduct Essentials: Inside Information, Conflicts and Personal Dealing
summary: A six-module foundation programme helping all staff handle inside information, personal dealing, gifts and communications correctly and avoid market abuse.
intro: This training programme equips all staff in a regulated firm to handle inside information properly, avoid market abuse, comply with personal dealing and gifts rules, and communicate and keep records in line with the firm's obligations.

sections.Aim and Purpose: To give staff at every level a clear, practical understanding of the market conduct rules that apply to them personally, not only to traders and dealers. Participants leave able to recognise inside information, avoid prohibited dealing and disclosure, manage gifts and communications correctly and report concerns promptly.
sections.What It Covers: Market integrity, inside information and market abuse, information barriers and insider lists, personal account dealing, gifts, hospitality and inducements, approved communication channels and recordkeeping, and responsible use of social media.
Intended Audience: All staff in regulated firms, including those outside trading and investment roles who may come across inside information
Front-office, research, operations, technology, marketing, HR and executive support staff
Line managers responsible for approving personal dealing, gifts and communications in their teams
Learning Objectives: Explain what inside information is and how staff in any role may come across it
Recognise insider dealing, unlawful disclosure and market manipulation
Apply the firm's personal account dealing rules and pre-clearance processes
Manage gifts, hospitality and inducements in line with the firm's policy
Use only approved communication channels and meet recordkeeping requirements
Use social media responsibly and escalate market conduct concerns promptly
sections.Structure and Format: Six modules of about ninety minutes each, delivered in person, virtually or in a hybrid format, either as a one- to two-day programme or as a series of short live sessions, and well suited to conversion into e-learning. Modules combine short briefings with real-world examples and scenario questions, work well as annual refresher training, and can be selected or tailored to the firm's policies and business.
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: No prior knowledge of markets or regulation is required. The programme is relevant to all staff, not only those in trading or investment roles.
Core Reading: IOSCO (2017), Objectives and Principles of Securities Regulation
IOSCO (2003), Insider Trading: How Jurisdictions Regulate It
FSB (2018), Strengthening Governance Frameworks to Mitigate Misconduct Risk: A Toolkit for Firms and Supervisors

modules.title: Market Integrity and Why It Matters to Everyone
modules.summary: Why fair and orderly markets matter, how market abuse harms investors and the firm, and why market conduct rules reach staff well beyond the trading floor.
objectives: Explain the purpose of market conduct rules and the harm market abuse causes
Recognise how staff in non-trading roles can be exposed to market conduct risk
Describe the consequences of breaches for individuals and the firm
syllabus: Fair, orderly and transparent markets and investor confidence
Who the rules apply to: staff, contractors and connected persons
Surveillance, investigations and enforcement outcomes
Personal consequences: criminal, civil and employment sanctions

modules.title: Inside Information and Market Abuse
modules.summary: What inside information is, how it is controlled through information barriers and insider lists, and the behaviours that amount to insider dealing, unlawful disclosure and market manipulation.
objectives: Identify inside information and the situations in which staff may receive it
Recognise insider dealing, unlawful disclosure and market manipulation
Apply information barrier, wall-crossing and insider list procedures
syllabus: What makes information inside information: precise, non-public and price-sensitive
Information barriers, wall-crossing and insider lists
Insider dealing, unlawful disclosure and market manipulation
Spotting and reporting suspicious orders and transactions

modules.title: Personal Account Dealing
modules.summary: The rules on staff dealing for themselves and connected persons, why pre-clearance and holding periods exist, and how to avoid conflicts and front running.
objectives: Explain the purpose and scope of the firm's personal account dealing policy
Apply pre-clearance, holding period and reporting requirements
Recognise dealing that creates conflicts of interest or market abuse risk
syllabus: Accounts, instruments and connected persons covered by the rules
Pre-clearance, restricted lists, holding periods and disclosure
Front running, derivatives, crypto-assets and other grey areas
Monitoring, breaches and what happens when things go wrong

modules.title: Gifts, Hospitality and Inducements
modules.summary: How gifts, hospitality and other benefits can create conflicts, improper inducements or bribery risk, and how to apply the firm's thresholds, approvals and registers.
objectives: Distinguish acceptable hospitality from improper inducements
Apply the firm's thresholds, approval and register requirements
Recognise when a gift or benefit creates a conflict of interest
syllabus: Gifts, hospitality, entertainment and non-monetary benefits
Inducements and their effect on independence and customer outcomes
Thresholds, pre-approval and the gifts and hospitality register
Red flags: frequency, timing, value and links to business decisions

modules.title: Communications and Recordkeeping
modules.summary: Why the firm must record and retain business communications, the risks of unapproved channels such as personal messaging apps, and how to communicate professionally and accurately.
objectives: Explain why business communications are recorded and retained
Use only approved channels for business communications
Communicate accurately and professionally, knowing that messages may be reviewed
syllabus: Recording obligations for calls, messages and electronic communications
Off-channel communications: personal devices and messaging apps
Retention, retrieval and supervisory review of records
Writing as if it will be read aloud: tone, accuracy and rumours

modules.title: Social Media, Public Statements and Practical Scenarios
modules.summary: How personal and professional use of social media can create market abuse, confidentiality, financial promotion and reputational risk, closing with practical market conduct scenarios.
objectives: Apply the firm's social media and public statements policy
Recognise how online posts can spread rumours, disclose information or amount to promotions
Apply the programme to realistic market conduct scenarios
syllabus: Personal and professional accounts: what you can and cannot say
Rumours, market commentary and amplifying unverified information
Financial promotions, endorsements and online influencers
Workshop: what would you do? Market conduct dilemmas
